text:
sahil: heads up — seeing a weird perf regression on the new batching heuristic when KV cache warms. latency spikes around kernel switchovers. starting nsys captures now, any quick flags I should use?

anna: +1. can you capture both traced kernels and NVTX brackets? that helps map batches -> kvcache ops.

sahil: plan: short deep capture covering warmup + steady state. trying to avoid huge files. my current command: 
```
nsys profile -o out/deep_batch_kv --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-duration=40s --sample=100us --force-overwrite --sample-cpu=none \\
  -- ./bin/runtime_bench --cfg cfg/batch_kv.json --runs 3
```
reasoning: cuda+nvtx for kernel timelines, osrt for OS runtime sampling to catch thread scheduling pauses, nvtx-brackets around high-level routing/batching.

jeff: looks reasonable. couple things: 1) sample rate 100us might blow up file size if kernels are tiny — consider 1ms for steady-state and bracketed 100us for warmup. 2) use nvtx brackets like `NVTX_PUSH("batch_start")` around batching decision + `NVTX_PUSH("kv_lookup")` — then capture-range=nvtx will let you bracket precisely.

lina: also instrument the kernel-selection path with a light `TRACEPOINT` so we can see the exact model variant switch. sometimes the kernel selector flips to a quantized path for short sequences and that creates odd microbursts.

sahil: good call. adding extra NVTX tags and a tracepoint. capturing two runs: warmup-only (20s) + long (60s) for steady. will annotate with exact seed.

anna: when you upload the `.qdrep`, can you include a tiny perfetto export for the CPU timeline? perfetto + nsys often helps pinpoint OS preemption vs GPU stalls. also attach the batching histogram from runtime (tokens/ms) — even a tiny CSV is useful.

jeff: if you see recurring small gaps in the kernel timeline that line up with KV evictions, check the eviction path locking — we recently added a spinloop that can backpressure scheduling. grep logs for `kvcache:evict` timestamps and correlate.

sahil: quick paste of a log snippet where spike happens: 
```
[00:12:34.512] batch_size=8 deciding->route=A kernel=matmul_f16
[00:12:34.530] kv:lookup hit latency=0.2ms
[00:12:34.532] kernel=matmul_q8 fallback_to=matmul_f16 time=+18ms  <-- big jump
[00:12:34.551] batch_emit tokens=128 latency=22ms
```
looks like kernel decision changed mid-batch.

lina: that 18ms is suspicious. could be kernel launch overhead + recompilation path. do you have persistent kernel cache enabled? on some drivers first launch does JIT. enable persistent kernel cache or warm the path with a dummy run.

jeff: another trick: run a focused capture on a single mini-batch with `--capture-range=nvtx:batch_start:batch_end` so file size is tiny and the timeline is easy to inspect.

sahil: will try: `nsys profile -o out/quick_mini --trace=cuda,nvtx -c nvtx --capture-range=nvtx:batch_start:batch_end --sample=1ms -- ./bin/runtime_bench --mini-batch` — is that `-c nvtx` right? i always forget shorthand.

anna: shorthand varies by nsys version. `--capture-range=nvtx` + NVTX push/pop is portable. if you need exact flags i can drop the versioned command. also ping `@eng-runtime` for a quick eyeball after upload. :eyes:  

nsys-bot: automated note: your profile `out/deep_batch_kv.qdrep` was uploaded to the shared bucket at s3://redwood-nsys/traces/2370012345/deep_batch_kv.qdrep (size: 420MB). Perf summary: 3 kernels dominated 82% of GPU time; OS runtime sampling shows intermittent 1-2ms CPU stalls.

sahil: thanks, uploaded both warmup and steady. attaching batching histogram and seed. will start correlating kvcache evict logs next.

lina: great — once we have the `.qdrep` i'll take a first pass on kernel-level timeline (matmul vs matmul_q8) and check if the quantized kernel exhibits a much higher launch overhead for short sequences. if so, we can change the kernel selector to prefer stable kernel for small batches.

jeff: keep an eye on the combined metric: tokens/ms during kernel switch vs steady. if kernel change reduces tokens/ms by >10% for more than 2 consecutive batches, that's a regression that needs a rollout hold.

sahil: noted. i'll post findings by EOD with a short perf table and the nsys extracts. thanks all.
